statement: Ro Khanna, a Democratic member of the US House from California, was visiting the occupied West Bank when his group was stopped and held.
Armed Israeli settlers first stopped his vehicle, and Israeli soldiers arrived afterward.
The incident happened near the Palestinian village of Khirbet Zanuta, in the southern West Bank hills.
The group was let go after calls were made to the US embassy in Jerusalem.
Khanna accused the Israeli military of lying about the detention.
The Israel Defense Forces said its soldiers dispersed the civilians and reopened the road, and that its soldiers did not take part in blocking the road.
Khanna is 49 years old.
The hold lasted about 90 minutes (BBC) or more than an hour (Al Jazeera, PBS) — sources differ on the exact length.
Lindsey Graham, a Republican US senator, died at the age of 71.
His office said he died after a brief and sudden illness.
Preliminary findings from the District of Columbia medical examiner gave the cause of death as aortic dissection linked to heart disease.
Graham had represented South Carolina in the US Senate since 2003.
He was up for re-election in November 2026.
Graham was an early critic of Donald Trump but later became one of his closest allies.
The day before his death he had visited Ukraine and met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster is expected to appoint a temporary replacement for the vacant seat.
Graham was known as a foreign policy hawk, especially on Iran and Russia.
Trump reportedly called Graham one of the greatest people and senators he had ever known.
Mitch McConnell is an 84-year-old Republican senator from Kentucky.
McConnell said for the first time on Sunday that a fall led to his hospitalization, breaking weeks of silence about his condition.
He was also treated for mild pneumonia and had been absent from Congress for weeks during the hospitalization.
Doctors ran a battery of tests to work out what caused the fall.
McConnell said he was regaining his strength but would not return to work quite yet.
McConnell said tests confirmed he did not break any bones or suffer a concussion, and did not have a heart attack or a stroke.
McConnell was hospitalized on June 14 and is now in a rehabilitation facility.
South Korea's exports rose 53.9 percent from a year earlier in the first 10 days of July (July 1-10).
The gain was driven mainly by strong semiconductor (chip) shipments.
Outbound shipments reached $29.8 billion in the July 1-10 period, up from $19.3 billion in the same period last year.
The figure was the highest for any 10-day period recorded by the customs agency; the previous record was $28.6 billion.
The data came from the Korea Customs Service.
Semiconductor exports nearly tripled to $11.2 billion.
Imports rose 17.4 percent to $23.5 billion, leaving a trade surplus of $6.4 billion for the period.
Exports to China rose 88.7 percent to $7 billion and exports to the United States rose 43.2 percent to $4.91 billion.
South Korea's Kospi index fell more than 20% from its June record high, entering bear market territory in early-to-mid July 2026.
The selloff was led by chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, whose shares fell sharply on worries about AI spending.
Samsung and SK hynix together make up around half of the Kospi's total weight, up from about a quarter at the end of the previous year, leaving the market heavily exposed to the AI chip trade.
The falls came despite strong earnings from the chipmakers, as investors focused instead on doubts about the long-term AI spending of big tech customers.
SK hynix raised $26.5 billion in a US listing, the largest-ever US IPO by a foreign company, surpassing Alibaba's $25 billion debut in 2014.
SK hynix sold 177.9 million American depositary shares at $149 each on Nasdaq, and the offering was more than seven times oversubscribed.
SK hynix's dollar inflow from the listing was expected to help bolster South Korea's foreign exchange market.
The European Commission issued preliminary findings on July 10, 2026, saying Meta's Facebook and Instagram breach the EU's Digital Services Act because of their addictive design.
The Commission named specific design features as harmful, including infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications and highly personalized recommendation algorithms.
The Commission said Meta failed to properly assess the risks these features pose to users' physical and mental well-being, including minors and vulnerable adults.
The Commission wants Meta to disable features such as autoplay and infinite scroll by default, add effective screen-time breaks, and make its recommendation systems less engagement-driven.
If the findings are confirmed, Meta could face a fine of up to 6% of its total worldwide annual turnover.
Existing safeguards, including time-management tools activated by default for teens, were judged ineffective because they can be easily dismissed and do not meaningfully reduce usage.
Meta rejected the findings, saying it disagreed with them and that they did not accurately reflect the steps the company has taken to protect teens.
Based on Meta's 2025 revenue, a maximum fine could exceed 12 billion dollars (about 11 billion euros).
On July 10, 2026, China recovered the first-stage booster of an orbital rocket for the first time, becoming the second country after SpaceX to bring an orbital-class booster back.
The rocket was launched by China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC), the country's state-owned space company.
Instead of landing on legs the way SpaceX does, the booster was caught by a net strung across a frame on a recovery ship at sea.
CASC said it plans to reuse the recovered booster before the end of 2026.
The rocket carried a satellite into its target orbit before the first stage came back down.
The rocket was the Long March 10B, and it lifted off from the Hainan Commercial Space Launch Site; the booster deployed four hooks to catch the net.
The booster carries roughly the same payload as SpaceX's Falcon 9.
Matin Kim, a Korean fashion brand, is reported to be releasing a collaboration collection with the KBO baseball team the LG Twins on July 20, 2026.
The collection is reported to include six clothing items, such as short-sleeve T-shirts and jumpers, plus five accessories, including bags, a ball cap, a beanie and a key ring.
Signature pieces reportedly include a dugout jacket and T-shirts printed with Matin Kim's doodle-style calligraphy of team-related keywords such as 'Jamsil Baseball Stadium' and 'Seoul'.

The collection is reported to be sold on Naver's Knockit platform (July 20-26), through a Naver Shopping Live broadcast at noon on July 20, and at the Matin Kim flagship store in Seongsu-dong, eastern Seoul, from July 24.
A fire broke out at a popular pub in Bangkok, Thailand.
At least 27 people were killed in the fire.
The pub was in the Chatuchak district, near the famous Chatuchak Weekend Market.
About 63 people were injured, many of them seriously.
Firefighters arrived to find customers running through the flames to escape.
The pub was named Na Ladprao and stood in the northern part of the Thai capital.
Authorities are investigating whether the pub had enough escape routes.
The United States launched a new wave of strikes on Iran.
The US said the strikes were aimed at degrading Iran's ability to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US insisted the Strait of Hormuz remained open, while Iran said it had closed the strait.
Iran launched wide-ranging attacks on US allies and bases in the region.
A ceasefire deal reached in June has been fraying, with several days of tit-for-tat strikes.
President Trump declared the waterway open to commercial traffic despite Iran's announcement of closure.
Iran responded to earlier US action by striking sites in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and Oman.
About 140 Iranian military targets were struck in earlier US action.
